International football competition

The **2021 Copa CONMEBOL Libertadores** was the 62nd edition of the [CONMEBOL Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") (also referred to as the *Copa Libertadores*), [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America")'s premier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organized by [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

Starting from this season, teams must be in the top division of their member association to play in South American club competitions,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-2) except for teams which are champions of the qualifying tournaments or cups.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-3)

On 14 May 2020, CONMEBOL announced the candidate venues for the 2021, 2022 and 2023 club competition finals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-5) On 13 May 2021, CONMEBOL announced that the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_Final "2021 Copa Libertadores Final") would be played at the [Estadio Centenario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Centenario "Estadio Centenario") in [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo"), Uruguay on 20 November 2021,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-6) but on 27 July 2021 the final was eventually confirmed to have been rescheduled to 27 November 2021.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-7)

Defending champions [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedade_Esportiva_Palmeiras "Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras") won their third Copa Libertadores title after beating fellow Brazilian club [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo "Clube de Regatas do Flamengo") by a 2–1 score after extra time in the final match.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-8) As winners of the 2021 Copa Libertadores, Palmeiras qualified for the [2021 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2021 FIFA Club World Cup"), and earned the right to play against the winners of the [2021 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana "2021 Copa Sudamericana") in the [2022 Recopa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Recopa_Sudamericana "2022 Recopa Sudamericana"). They also automatically qualified for the [2022 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Copa_Libertadores "2022 Copa Libertadores") group stage.

## Teams

The following 47 teams from the 10 CONMEBOL member associations qualified for the tournament:[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-slots_final-9)

- Copa Libertadores champions
- Copa Sudamericana champions
- Brazil: 7 berths
- Argentina: 6 berths
- All other associations: 4 berths each

The entry stage was determined as follows:[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-slots_final-9)

- Group stage: 28 teams
  - Copa Libertadores champions
  - Copa Sudamericana champions
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–5 from Argentina and Brazil
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–2 from all other associations
- Second stage: 13 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berths 6–7 from Brazil
  - Team which qualified for berth 6 from Argentina
  - Teams which qualified for berths 3–4 from Chile and Colombia
  - Teams which qualified for berth 3 from all other associations
- First stage: 6 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berth 4 from Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela

Notes

1.  
  **Argentina (ARG):**
  - On 28 April 2020, the [Argentine Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Football_Association "Argentine Football Association") announced the abandonment of the [2020 Copa de la Superliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_de_la_Superliga "2020 Copa de la Superliga") and the culmination of the 2019–20 season due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina"). The six Argentina berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores were awarded to the following:[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-13)
    - The *Argentina 1* berth was awarded to the [2019–20 Superliga Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Argentine_Primera_División "2019–20 Argentine Primera División") champions.
    - The *Argentina 2* berth, originally awarded to the 2020 Copa de la Superliga champions, was awarded to the winner of a tournament to be played in the second semester of 2020, later confirmed to be the [2020 Copa de la Liga Profesional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_de_la_Liga_Profesional "2020 Copa de la Liga Profesional").
    - The *Argentina 3* berth was awarded to the [2019–20 Copa Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Copa_Argentina "2019–20 Copa Argentina") champions, provided that government directives allowed for it to be concluded.
    - The *Argentina 4*, *Argentina 5*, and *Argentina 6* berths were awarded to the three best teams of the [2019–20 Superliga Argentina and 2020 Copa de la Superliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Argentine_Primera_División#International_qualification "2019–20 Argentine Primera División") aggregate table at the time of the suspension of the latter competition not yet qualified.
  - On 11 December 2020 it was confirmed that the 2019–20 Copa Argentina would not be completed in time to award its winner a berth into the 2021 Copa Libertadores, therefore the *Argentina 3* berth was reallocated to the best team of the 2019–20 Superliga Argentina and 2020 Copa de la Superliga aggregate table not yet qualified.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-14)

2.  
  **Bolivia (BOL):** The 2020 Clausura tournament was not held due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia"), therefore the *Bolivia 2*, *Bolivia 3*, and *Bolivia 4* berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores were reallocated to the [2020 Apertura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Bolivian_Primera_División_season#Torneo_Apertura "2020 Bolivian Primera División season") runners-up, third and fourth-placed teams, respectively.

3.  
  **Chile (CHI):** On 30 December 2020, the Council of Presidents of the [ANFP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asociación_Nacional_de_Fútbol_Profesional "Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional") decided that the *Chile 4* berth, originally awarded to the [2020 Copa Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_Chile?action=edit&redlink=1 "2020 Copa Chile (page does not exist)") champions, would be awarded to the fourth-placed team of the [2020 Chilean Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Chilean_Primera_División "2020 Chilean Primera División"), given that the 2020 Copa Chile would not be held before the start of the 2021 Copa Libertadores.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-15)

4.  
  **Colombia (COL):**
  - On 25 July 2020, [DIMAYOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/División_Mayor_del_Fútbol_Profesional_Colombiano "División Mayor del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano") decided that the [2020 Categoría Primera A season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Categoría_Primera_A_season "2020 Categoría Primera A season"), suspended from 13 March due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia"), would only have a single tournament played for the remainder of the season. Therefore, the *Colombia 1* berth of the 2021 Copa Libertadores, originally awarded to the 2020 Apertura champions, and the *Colombia 2* berth, originally awarded to the 2020 Finalización champions, would instead be awarded to the champions and runners-up of that single tournament, respectively.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-16)
  - On 9 September 2020, DIMAYOR confirmed the reallocation of the four Colombia berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores as follows:[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-17)
    - The *Colombia 1* berth was awarded to the 2020 Primera A champions.
    - The *Colombia 2* berth was awarded to the 2020 Primera A runners-up.
    - The *Colombia 3* berth was awarded to the [2020 Primera A aggregate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Categoría_Primera_A_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Categoría Primera A season") best team not yet qualified.
    - The *Colombia 4* berth, originally awarded to the [2020 Copa Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_Colombia "2020 Copa Colombia") champions, was awarded to the 2020 Primera A aggregate table 2nd best team not yet qualified.

5.  
  **Uruguay (URU):** Given that the [2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") was not concluded before the start of the [2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_qualifying_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay "COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay"), on 14 January 2021 the League Council of the [Uruguayan Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguayan_Football_Association "Uruguayan Football Association") approved a temporary modification to the qualification method of Uruguayan teams. Since associations had to formally inform CONMEBOL of the teams that would take part in international competition ahead of the start of competition, some international berths were decided based on deadlines set according to the dates the respective Copa Libertadores rounds were scheduled for as well as the placements of teams in the [2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") aggregate table at the time of those deadlines:[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-18)
  - The *Uruguay 4* berth was awarded to the best eligible team of the 2020 Primera División aggregate table as of 7 February 2021, considering that the Copa Libertadores first stage was scheduled to begin on 23 February 2021. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._(Montevideo) "Liverpool F.C. (Montevideo)") ([2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") aggregate table fifth place as of 7 February 2021) accepted the berth after the top four of the aggregate table at that moment ([Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Nacional_de_Football "Club Nacional de Football"), [Montevideo City Torque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo_City_Torque "Montevideo City Torque"), [Peñarol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peñarol "Peñarol"), and [Rentistas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.A._Rentistas "C.A. Rentistas")) all declined to take the berth.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-19)
  - The *Uruguay 3* berth was awarded to the best eligible team of the 2020 Primera División aggregate table as of 21 February 2021, considering that the Copa Libertadores second stage was scheduled to begin on 9 March 2021. [Montevideo Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo_Wanderers_F.C. "Montevideo Wanderers F.C.") (2020 Primera División aggregate table fifth place as of 21 February 2021) accepted the berth after the top three of the aggregate table at that moment (Nacional, Montevideo City Torque, and Peñarol) all declined to take the berth, and fourth-placed Liverpool was already qualified as *Uruguay 4*.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-20)
  - Teams were offered the chance to accept or decline the berths they were eligible for at the time of the respective deadlines.

6.  
  **Venezuela (VEN):** On 15 May 2020, the [Venezuelan Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_Football_Federation "Venezuelan Football Federation") decided the permanent suspension of the [2020 Venezuelan Primera División season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Venezuelan_Primera_División_season "2020 Venezuelan Primera División season") and the voiding of the standings and results recorded due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Venezuela "COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-22) The allocation of the four Venezuela berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores would be announced at a later time, with the FVF confirming a will to organize a new tournament in which sporting merit, club licensing requirements, and medical protocols were applied.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-23) The definitive berth allocations were confirmed by the FVF on 18 September 2020.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-24)

Teams were seeded by their *CONMEBOL Clubs ranking* as of 1 February 2021 (shown in parentheses),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-ranking-33) taking into account the following three factors:[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-34)

1. Performance in the last 10 years, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 2011–2020.
2. Historical coefficient, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 1960–2010 and 2002-2010 respectively.
3. Local tournament champion, with bonus points awarded to domestic league champions of the last 10 years

For the first stage, the six teams were drawn into three ties (E1–E3), with the teams from Pot 1 hosting the second leg.

For the third stage, the eight winners of the second stage were allocated without any draw into the following four ties (G1–G4), with the team in each tie with the higher CONMEBOL ranking hosting the second leg. As their identity was not known at the time of the draw, they could be drawn into the same tie with another team from the same association.

- Second stage winner C1 vs. Second stage winner C8
- Second stage winner C2 vs. Second stage winner C7
- Second stage winner C3 vs. Second stage winner C6
- Second stage winner C4 vs. Second stage winner C5

The draw for the group stage was held on 9 April 2021, 12:00 [PYT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Paraguay "Time in Paraguay") ([UTC−4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC−04:00 "UTC−04:00")), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [Luque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luque "Luque"), [Paraguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay "Paraguay").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-Group_stage_draw-29)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-35) For the group stage, the 32 teams were drawn into eight groups (Groups A–H) of four containing a team from each of the four pots. Teams from the same association could not be drawn into the same group, excluding the four winners of the third stage, which were seeded in Pot 4 and whose identity was not known at the time of the draw, and could be drawn into the same group with another team from the same association.

## Qualifying stages

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_qualifying_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages")

In the qualifying stages, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis. If tied on aggregate, the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was used. If still tied, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.3).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1) The qualifying stages were structured as follows:

- **First stage (6 teams):** The three winners of the first stage advanced to the second stage to join the 13 teams which were given byes to the second stage.
- **Second stage (16 teams):** The eight winners of the second stage advanced to the third stage.
- **Third stage (8 teams):** The four winners of the third stage advanced to the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_group_stage "2021 Copa Libertadores group stage") to join the 28 direct entrants. The four teams eliminated in the third stage entered the [Copa Sudamericana group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana_group_stage "2021 Copa Sudamericana group stage").

## Group stage

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_group_stage "2021 Copa Libertadores group stage")

In the group stage, each group is played on a home-and-away [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament") basis. The teams are ranked according to the following criteria: 1. [Points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, and 0 points for a loss); 2. [Goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference"); 3. Goals scored; 4. Away goals scored; 5. CONMEBOL ranking (Regulations Article 2.4.2).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

The winners and runners-up of each group advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages#Round_of_16 "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages") of the [final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages"). The third-placed teams of each group entered the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana_final_stages#Round_of_16 "2021 Copa Sudamericana final stages") of the [2021 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana "2021 Copa Sudamericana").

## Final stages

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages")

Starting from the round of 16, the teams played a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") with the following rules:[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

- In the round of 16, quarter-finals and semi-finals, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis, with the higher-seeded team hosting the second leg (Regulations Article 2.2.3.2). If tied on aggregate, the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was used. If still tied, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.3).
- The final was played as a single match at a venue pre-selected by CONMEBOL, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes (Regulations Article 2.2.3.5). If tied after regulation, 30 minutes of extra time were played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.4).

# Copa Libertadores da América de 2023

*Copa Libertadores da América de 2023*

| LXIV Copa Libertadores de América   CONMEBOL Libertadores 2023 | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/pt/thumb/9/95/Conmebol_Libertadores_logo.svg/250px-Conmebol_Libertadores_logo.svg.png?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Conmebol_Libertadores_logo.svg) | |
| Detalhes | |

| Colocações finais | |
| Campeão | **[Fluminense](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluminense_Football_Club "Fluminense Football Club") (1.º título)** |

| Melhor ataque (fase inicial) | [Palmeiras](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedade_Esportiva_Palmeiras "Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras") – 16 gols |
| Melhor defesa (fase inicial) | [Boca Juniors](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Boca_Juniors "Club Atlético Boca Juniors") – 2 gols |
| Maiores goleadas    (diferença) | [Nacional Potosí](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Nacional_Potosí "Club Atlético Nacional Potosí") 1–6 [El Nacional](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Deportivo_El_Nacional "Club Deportivo El Nacional")   [Estádio Hernando Siles](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_Hernando_Siles "Estádio Hernando Siles"), [La Paz](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Paz "La Paz")   8 de fevereiro, [primeira fase](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fases_preliminares_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023#Chave_E2 "Fases preliminares da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")  ---  [Melgar](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot_Ball_Club_Melgar "Foot Ball Club Melgar") 5–0 [Patronato](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Patronato "Club Atlético Patronato")   [Estádio Monumental da UNSA](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_Monumental_da_UNSA "Estádio Monumental da UNSA"), [Arequipa](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arequipa "Arequipa")   6 de junho, [grupo H](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_de_grupos_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023#Grupo_H "Fase de grupos da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023") |
| Premiações | |
| Melhor jogador | *prêmio cancelado*[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-1) |
| ← [2022](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2022 "Copa Libertadores da América de 2022")   [2024](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2024 "Copa Libertadores da América de 2024") → | |

A **[Copa Libertadores da América](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América "Copa Libertadores da América") de [2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023 "2023")**, oficialmente **CONMEBOL Libertadores 2023**, foi a 64.ª edição da competição de futebol realizada anualmente pela [Confederação Sul-Americana de Futebol](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederação_Sul-Americana_de_Futebol "Confederação Sul-Americana de Futebol") (CONMEBOL). Participaram clubes das dez associações sul-americanas.

Em 8 de março, a CONMEBOL anunciou que a partida final da competição seria disputada no [estádio do Maracanã](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_Jornalista_Mário_Filho "Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho"), no [Rio de Janeiro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro").[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-2) Inicialmente marcada para ocorrer em 11 de novembro, foi antecipada em uma semana, passando para 4 de novembro.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-finaldata-3)

O [Fluminense](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluminense_Football_Club "Fluminense Football Club") conquistou o seu primeiro título na competição ao superar o [Boca Juniors](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Boca_Juniors "Club Atlético Boca Juniors") na [final](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023") por 2–1, após a [prorrogação](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prorrogação "Prorrogação").[[4]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-4) Com isso, teve o direito de enfrentar o campeão da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023") na [Recopa Sul-Americana de 2024](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recopa_Sul-Americana_de_2024 "Recopa Sul-Americana de 2024"), assim como se classificou automaticamente para a fase de grupos da [Copa Libertadores da América de 2024](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2024 "Copa Libertadores da América de 2024") e para a [Copa do Mundo de Clubes de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_do_Mundo_de_Clubes_da_FIFA_de_2023 "Copa do Mundo de Clubes da FIFA de 2023") e o [Mundial de Clubes de 2025](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundial_de_Clubes_FIFA_de_2025 "Mundial de Clubes FIFA de 2025").

## Equipes classificadas

As seguintes 47 equipes das 10 federações filiadas à CONMEBOL se qualificaram para o torneio:[[5]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-5)

- Campeão da Copa Libertadores da América de 2022
- Campeão da Copa Sul-Americana de 2022
- Brasil: 7 vagas
- Argentina: 6 vagas
- Demais associações: 4 vagas cada

A fase de entrada é determinada da seguinte maneira:

- **Fase de grupos: 28 equipes**
  - Campeão da Copa Libertadores de 2022;
  - Campeão da Copa Sul-Americana de 2022;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 1 a 5 da Argentina e do Brasil;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 1 e 2 de todas as outras associações.
- **Segunda fase: 13 equipes**
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 6 e 7 do Brasil;
  - Equipe que qualificou para a vaga 6 da Argentina;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 3 e 4 do Chile e Colômbia;
  - Equipes qualificadas para a vaga 3 de todas as outras associações.
- **Primeira fase: 6 equipes**
  - Equipes que se qualificaram para a vaga 4 da Bolívia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela.

## Premiação financeira

Em 17 de março, a CONMEBOL anunciou uma mudança na premiação em dinheiro da competição. A partir desta edição, os clubes foram premiados por cada vitória na fase de grupos. O valor pago, por vitória, foi de 300 mil [dólares](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dólar_dos_Estados_Unidos "Dólar dos Estados Unidos") — cerca de 1,5 milhão de [reais](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_(moeda_brasileira) "Real (moeda brasileira)"). Conforme o comunicado da entidade, o objetivo é "*reconhecer os méritos esportivos*". Também houve um aumento nos valores das premiações em cerca de 23 [por cento](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcentagem "Porcentagem") em relação a edição do ano passado e a competição distribuiu 207 milhões de dólares ou cerca de 1,087 bilhão de reais.[[6]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-7)

## Fases preliminares

Ver artigo principal: [Fases preliminares da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fases_preliminares_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fases preliminares da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Nas fases preliminares cada emparelhamento foi definido em partidas eliminatórias de ida e volta. Em caso de empate no placar agregado, a vaga seria definida direto na [disputa por pênaltis](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disputa_por_pênaltis "Disputa por pênaltis"), sem prorrogação. Os confrontos das duas primeiras fases foram definidos através de sorteio.[[14]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulam-15)

- **Primeira fase:** disputada por seis equipes provenientes de Bolívia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela, qualifica três para a seguinte fase.
- **Segunda fase:** disputada por 16 equipes, sendo 13 delas provenientes de Argentina, Bolívia, Brasil, Chile, Colômbia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela mais os três vencedores da fase anterior, qualifica oito equipes para a seguinte fase.
- **Terceira fase:** disputada pelas oito equipes vencedoras da fase anterior, as quatro vencedoras avançam para a fase de grupos com as outras 28 equipes e a quatro perdedoras sendo transferidas para a [fase de grupos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_de_grupos_da_Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Fase de grupos da Copa Sul-Americana de 2023") da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023").

## Fase de grupos

Ver artigo principal: [Fase de grupos da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_de_grupos_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fase de grupos da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Os vencedores e os segundos classificados de cada grupo avançam para as oitavas de final, enquanto os terceiros colocados foram transferidos para os *play-offs* da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023").

Nessa fase, cada grupo é disputado em turno e returno, todos contra todos. As equipes são classificadas de acordo com os seguintes critérios:[[14]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulam-15)

1. Pontos (três pontos por vitória, um ponto por empate e nenhum ponto por derrota)
2. Saldo de gols
3. Gols marcados
4. Gols marcados fora de casa
5. [Ranking CONMEBOL](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranking_CONMEBOL "Ranking CONMEBOL")

## Fase final

Ver artigo principal: [Fase final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_final_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fase final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Após a conclusão da fase de grupos, um sorteio, em 5 de julho — na sede da CONMEBOL, em Luque, no Paraguai — definiu o chaveamento das equipes classificadas a partir das oitavas de final até a final.[[15]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulamento-16)[[11]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-uol_definido_sorteio_oitavas-11)

As equipes que finalizaram em primeiro lugar na fase de grupos (pote 1 no sorteio) enfrentam as equipes que finalizaram em segundo lugar (pote 2), não havendo restrições nos confrontos, portanto podendo ser sorteadas equipes de um mesmo país ou que integraram o mesmo grupo na fase anterior. A pontuação obtida na fase de grupos serve para a definição dos mandos de campo até a semifinal, com as equipes melhores posicionadas sempre realizando o jogo de volta como equipe mandante, sendo numeradas de 1 a 16.[[15]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulamento-16)[[11]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-uol_definido_sorteio_oitavas-11)

International football competition

The **2025 Copa CONMEBOL Libertadores** was the 66th edition of the [CONMEBOL Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") (also referred to as the *Copa Libertadores*), [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America")'s premier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organized by [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL"). The competition began on 4 February and ended on 29 November 2025,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-1) with [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_final "2025 Copa Libertadores final") played at [Estadio Monumental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Monumental_"U" "Estadio Monumental "U"") in [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima"), Peru.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-3)

Brazilian club [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CR_Flamengo "CR Flamengo") won their fourth Copa Libertadores title, defeating fellow Brazilian side [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SE_Palmeiras "SE Palmeiras") 1–0 in the final.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-4) As winners of the 2025 Copa Libertadores, Flamengo earned the right to play against the winners of the [2025 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Sudamericana "2025 Copa Sudamericana") in the [2026 Recopa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Recopa_Sudamericana "2026 Recopa Sudamericana"). They also automatically qualified for the [2025 FIFA Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Intercontinental_Cup "2025 FIFA Intercontinental Cup"), the [2029 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2029_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2029 FIFA Club World Cup") and the [2026 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Copa_Libertadores "2026 Copa Libertadores") group stage.

[Botafogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botafogo_de_Futebol_e_Regatas "Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas") were the defending champions, but were eliminated by [LDU Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.D.U._Quito "L.D.U. Quito") in the round of 16.

With Flamengo's triumph, Brazil tied Argentina as the nation with the most Copa Libertadores championships with 25 titles. This was as well the seventh consecutive edition won by Brazilian clubs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-5)

## Teams

The following 47 teams from the 10 CONMEBOL member associations qualified for the tournament:

- Copa Libertadores champions
- Copa Sudamericana champions
- Brazil: 7 berths
- Argentina: 6 berths
- All other associations: 4 berths each

The entry stage was determined as follows:[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-6)

- Group stage: 28 teams
  - Copa Libertadores champions
  - Copa Sudamericana champions
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–5 from Argentina and Brazil
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–2 from all other associations
- Second stage: 13 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berths 6–7 from Brazil
  - Team which qualified for berth 6 from Argentina
  - Teams which qualified for berths 3–4 from Chile and Colombia
  - Teams which qualified for berth 3 from all other associations
- First stage: 6 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berth 4 from Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela

The draw for the qualifying stages was held on 19 December 2024, 12:00 [PYT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Paraguay "Time in Paraguay") ([UTC−3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC−03:00 "UTC−03:00")), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [Luque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luque "Luque"), [Paraguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay "Paraguay").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-22)

Teams were seeded by their *CONMEBOL Clubs ranking* as of 16 December 2024 (shown in parentheses),[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-ranking-23) taking into account the following three factors:[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-24)

1. Performance in the last 10 years, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 2015–2024.
2. Historical coefficient, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 1960–2014 and 2002–2014 respectively.
3. Local tournament champion, with bonus points awarded to domestic league champions of the last 10 years.

For the first stage, the six teams were drawn into three ties (E1–E3), with the teams from Pot 1 hosting the second leg.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-draw_procedure-18)

- Second stage winner C1 vs. Second stage winner C8
- Second stage winner C2 vs. Second stage winner C7
- Second stage winner C3 vs. Second stage winner C6
- Second stage winner C4 vs. Second stage winner C5

For the group stage, the 32 teams were drawn into eight groups (Groups A–H) of four containing a team from each of the four pots. Teams from the same association could not be drawn into the same group, excluding the four winners of the third stage, which were allocated to Pot 4 and could be drawn into the same group with another team from the same association.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-25)

The draw for the round of 16 was held on 2 June 2025, 12:00 [PYT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Paraguay "Time in Paraguay") ([UTC−3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC−03:00 "UTC−03:00")) at the CONMEBOL headquarters in [Luque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luque "Luque"), Paraguay.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-26) For the round of 16, the 16 teams were drawn into eight ties (A–H) between a group winner (Pot 1) and a group runner-up (Pot 2), with the group winners hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association or the same group could be drawn into the same tie (Regulations Article 2.2.3.2).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-6)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-27)

## Qualifying stages

Main article: [2025 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_qualifying_stages "2025 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages")

In the qualifying stages, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis. If tied on aggregate, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.3).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-6) The qualifying stages were structured as follows:

- **First stage (6 teams):** The three winners of the first stage advanced to the second stage to join the 13 teams which were given byes to the second stage.
- **Second stage (16 teams):** The eight winners of the second stage advanced to the third stage.
- **Third stage (8 teams):** The four winners of the third stage advanced to the group stage to join the 28 direct entrants. The four teams eliminated in the third stage entered the [Copa Sudamericana group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Sudamericana_group_stage "2025 Copa Sudamericana group stage").

## Group stage

Main article: [2025 Copa Libertadores group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_group_stage "2025 Copa Libertadores group stage")

In the group stage, each group was played on a home-and-away [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament") basis. Teams were ranked according to the following criteria: 1. [Points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, and 0 points for a loss); 2. [Goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference"); 3. Goals scored; 4. Away goals scored; 5. CONMEBOL ranking (Regulations Article 2.4.2).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-6)

The winners and runners-up of each group advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages#Round_of_16 "2025 Copa Libertadores final stages") of the [final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2025 Copa Libertadores final stages"). The third-placed teams of each group entered the [knockout round play-offs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Sudamericana_final_stages#Knockout_round_play-offs "2025 Copa Sudamericana final stages") of the [2025 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Sudamericana "2025 Copa Sudamericana").

## Final stages

Main article: [2025 Copa Libertadores final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2025 Copa Libertadores final stages")

Starting from the round of 16, the teams played a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") with the following rules:[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-6)

- In the round of 16, quarter-finals and semi-finals, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis, with the higher-seeded team hosting the second leg (Regulations Article 2.2.3.2). If tied on aggregate, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.3).
- The final was played as a single match at a venue pre-selected by CONMEBOL, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes (Regulations Article 2.2.3.5). If tied after regulation, 30 minutes of extra time were played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.4).
